title: AnnotationSet freeze request
description:
The body of POST /api/v1/dataset-versions/{dataset_version_id}/annotation-sets, table 10.2-B row R29, against the permission annotation_set.create. This is MOS-UI-129's explicit close-the-campaign action: the console MUST state before it that a frozen set cannot be appended to and that adding a reader or a case afterwards produces a NEW set (MOS-TRAIN-110), which 0006_evidence enforces with annotation_sets_frozen and annotations_frozen and which medos/medos/evidence/repo.py enforces by having no add_reader() at all.

THERE IS NO PER-CASE ANNOTATION PAYLOAD IN THIS BODY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. medos/medos/evidence/repo.py::freeze_annotation_set takes its entries from its caller in-process; a route that forwarded a client's entries would let a caller supply a reference standard no reader produced, and MOS-EVID-038's named readers would then be an assertion rather than a record. MOS-TRAIN-096 requires every MONAI Label session to authenticate as a MedicalOS User precisely so that the set can name its readers after the fact, and MOS-TRAIN-095 puts the annotation surface inside the evidence-plane network reading through the Gateway. The store those sessions write into does not exist in this platform yet (ch. 19 section 19.4.3), which medos/api/v1/routes.train.yaml records in the comment on this row -- naming the gap is the alternative to closing it with a request member that would outlive it. (There is no engine_absent: key: measured on both registries, the rows carry engine: and engine_also: and the absences live in the row comments.)

`tool` is not a member either: MOS-UI-124 says the platform fills it from the deployed annotation stack and the operator does not type it. `reader_id` is a User principal and never a group, a rota, a shared login, a service account or an email address (MOS-UI-123): a shared account makes MOS-EVID-038 unsatisfiable after the fact.

name.description: Unique per DatasetVersion (annotation_sets_name_uk). A name and not a digest, because MOS-UI-101 forbids the operator composing one and MOS-UI-147 renders the reference standard in a read-only summary that has to say something a human recognises.

label_definition_id.description: MOS-EVID-143: a capability_concepts row (MOS-REG-042, MOS-STORE-256). Chosen from the capability's concepts rather than typed.

annotation_type.description: 0006_evidence's CHECK, mirrored. MOS-UI-128 and MOS-TRAIN-095 make mask, bounding_box and point the MONAI Label types; case_label and measurement are chapter 7's and are collected elsewhere.

consensus_rule.description: MOS-EVID-039's six-value enum, mirrored exactly from the column. MOS-UI-125 requires the console to have stated, when two or more readers were assigned, that inter-reader agreement will be computed and will appear in every report citing the set (MOS-EVID-043) -- a Dice of 0.82 against a reference whose own inter-reader Dice is 0.84 is a different claim from the same 0.82 against 0.97.

consensus_params.description: MOS-EVID-039's per-rule parameters: min_agreeing for majority_at_least_2; iterations, convergence_tol, initial_sensitivity, initial_specificity and rng_seed for staple; arbitrator_id for arbitrated. MOS-TRAIN-105 is why staple's five are mandatory -- the reduction MUST be reproducible from the persisted per-reader masks alone, and a tool-side reduction recording none of them cannot be re-derived. The per-rule requirement is checked by medos/medos/evidence/repo.py rather than here, because JSON Schema can express the conditional and cannot express that the checker and the database agree on it; both do, and the integration test is what holds them together.

readers.description: MOS-EVID-038: every AnnotationSet MUST name at least one reader, and a set with reader_count = 0 MUST be refused.

reference_of_record.description: MOS-EVID-042: if the only available reference standard is algorithmic, the reader role MUST be `algorithm` and this MUST be false. An AcceptanceCriteria gate refuses a set whose flag is false, which is the point at which an algorithmic reference stops being usable as a bar rather than the point at which it stops being recordable.

reader.title: Annotation reader
reader.description: MOS-UI-124's structured inputs, which the console MUST collect and MUST NOT invent parallel ones for (MOS-TRAIN-097).

reader_id.description: A MedicalOS User principal (MOS-UI-123, MOS-TRAIN-096). Never a group, a rota, a shared login, a service account or an email address.

blinded_to.description: MOS-EVID-038's reader table and MOS-TRAIN-097's field set: what this reader could not see. MOS-TRAIN-104 and MOS-UI-216 make blinding a property of the surface rather than of the instructions -- enforcement is the session grant failing to resolve the value, never a value the client holds and does not paint -- so an entry here is a record of how the session was configured and not a promise the reader made.
